tagline: Self-hosted file sync and sharing server written in Go, storing data on the filesystem with no database.
description: OpenCloud is a file sync and sharing server, written in Go and published under the Apache 2.0 licence. It is built as a single binary: you run an init command to create a configuration, then start the server. Users sign in through OpenID Connect, either with an external identity provider such as Keycloak or with the identity provider embedded in the server. The backend needs no database. Everything is written to the filesystem, by default under the home directory of the user running it. That keeps the moving parts few, but it also means your backup plan is a file backup plan. The repository README is aimed at contributors, so installation guidance for production lives in the separate documentation site. Our data lists no deploy method for it, and no hosted offer. As a replacement for Dropbox Plus it covers the core loop of storing files and sharing them with other people from your own server. Check the documentation for clients, office editing and sync behaviour before you commit, because the main repository only describes the server backend. The project was created in January 2025, so it has a shorter track record than older self-hosted file platforms.
strengths: Single Go binary that starts with two commands: init, then server
No database to install or tune; data is stored as files
Sign-in through OpenID Connect, with an embedded identity provider if you have none
Apache 2.0 licence, so the server code can be modified and redistributed freely
limits: No database means backups and growth planning depend on the filesystem you choose
The main repository documents only the backend; clients and production setup are described elsewhere
Needs an OpenID Connect provider for sign-in, either embedded or external
Young project, created in 2025, with a shorter history than older file-sync servers
bestFor: A small team with its own server that wants Dropbox-style file sharing without running a database.
